OriginalEnglish: Now you can switch characters in the heat of battle with <PD><FG>
UNUSED
Press <P0> when your tension gauge is full to go into high-tension mode for a limited time<FG>
UNUSED
As long as you're in high-tension mode, you'll be totally immune to damage<MV>and that's just for starters<FG>
Your attack power will also increase, and any status ailments will be cured instantly<FG>
And as if that wasn't enough, you'll also be able to use spells and abilities without spending a single point of MP<FG>
When you're done, press <P0> to unleash a coup de grâce and leave high-tension mode in style<FG>
UNUSED
If you ever want to exit an encounter instantly, cast Evac to make good your escape.
To access it, just open the menu. And don't worry<MV>you won't lose any items, gold or experience by beating an early retreat.
Allies who've fallen unconscious can be revived with an Yggdrasil leaf. To use one, approach a fallen friend and press <P1>.
Yggdrasil leaves are consumed upon use, but your stock will be replenished whenever you leave Accordia or enter a battle.
If you're beaten in battle, you can choose to start the fight over again from the beginning.
If you choose not to start over, you'll be taken back to a priestess.
In either case, you'll be allowed to keep any experience or gold coins you've earned.
When travelling to the War Zones where specific battles happen, you'll often go through open areas, otherwise known as Wild Zones.
When moving around in Wild Zones, things will change depending on whether or not you're currently in battle.
When monsters are nearby, you'll draw your weapons ready to fight, and when they're further off, you'll put your weapons away.
When you're in battle, only your MP will recharge, but out of battle, both HP and MP will be replenished.
You'll sometimes find floating jewels called Zoomstones out in the field.
Press <PL> to attune yourself to a Zoomstone, and you'll be able to travel there instantly from anywhere by casting Zoom.
When you're fighting a battle that carries on immediately from another one, you can choose to pop back for a pit stop in Accordia first.
You can take this opportunity to change your party line-up, equipment and skills, or to go shopping for any supplies you might need.
Once you've finished up in the capital, just cast Zoom to zip back to where battle awaits<FG>
When you're wandering around out in the wild, you'll occasionally come across people being attacked by monsters.
Perform your knightly duties by plucking these innocents from peril, and you'll earn extra experience<FG>
Every so often when you're out in the wild, you'll come across particularly powerful monsters.
Some of them won't let you get away without a fight, so make sure all your party members are prepared for the unexpected<FG>
Keep an eye out on the battlefield for beasties with their names above their heads. These are marked monsters, wanted by the authorities<FG>
They're tougher than the average enemy, but they'll also earn you lots of experience and exciting items<FG>
Your monster medal holder means you can catch and carry the coins that defeated enemies sometimes drop.
Monster medals allow you to call on a monster's particular powers whenever you like.
To unleash one, use <P5> to select it, then press <P9> to let it loose<FG>
Saviour-type monster medals summon minions to support you using their trademark moves.
But they'll disappear as soon as they're done, so be sure to save them for just the right moment.
Sentry-type medals summon minions to fight on your behalf until their health runs out.
They'll attack enemies in the immediate vicinity, and can also respond to specific situations, such as the need to protect people.
Substitute-type medals let you walk on the wild side by temporarily taking the form of a monster<FG>
You'll be able to use some amazing moves, but you won't be able to change character, so be sure to save them for when the time is right<FG>
The Zoom spell can instantly transport you to any of the Zoomstones to which you've previously attuned yourself.
To cast it, simply select it from the menu<MV>but bear in mind that you can't use it mid-battle, or when spells and abilities are unavailable.
Healstones can give you an instant mid-battle health boost. Just hold down <PP> and press <P9> to use one.
UNUSED
They'll be consumed upon use, but your stock will be replenished whenever you leave Accordia or enter a battle.
If you end up being beaten while out in a Wild Zone, you'll be transported back to a priestess with all the experience and gold you've earned.
A person's proficiency rating tells you how good they are with a given weapon. You can increase it by inflicting damage on enemies.
You can check your party members' proficiency with the various weapon types by looking under ‘Attributes’ in the menu.
And when you've earned enough, go and see the Martial Master in Accordia<MV>he might just have a thing or two to teach you<FG>
Party Powers are special skills that give you and your allies a boost. You can learn one for every five proficiency levels with a weapon.
There are different powers for each of the different weapon types, and they're shared with the whole party once learned.
To pick which Party Powers to use, you'll need to select ‘Skills’ from the menu.
Tag Tricks are special attacks you can carry out by pressing <PD> to change characters while holding <PP>.
UNUSED
These terrific techniques can have some amazing effects, but they can also cost a lot of MP, so use them with care<FG>
Characters will draw or sheathe their weapons depending on the situation.
Your weapons will be drawn if you perform any attacking actions, or if monsters appear nearby.
If you stop attacking for a short while, or if monsters are no longer close, your weapons will be sheathed.
You can run by pressing <PQ>, but only when your weapons are sheathed.
UNUSED
There are other actions, such as changing equipment, that can only be performed with your weapons put away.
Teleportals are a magical means of transport that can zip you from one place to another in an instant. Press <PL> when near one to use it.
<F4><S2> starts the adventure with a set of twin swords<MV>swift, versatile weapons known for their slicing, dicing combos.
With twin swords equipped, you can use the Cold Fission skill to swallow up whole swathes of foes in a wintry whirlwind<FG>
<F4><S3> starts the adventure with a sword and shield, orthodox adventuring arms suitable for any situation.
With a sword equipped, you can use the Inferno Slash skill to swallow up whole swathes of foes in a searing cyclone<FG>
Cesar wields a greatsword, and battles with both strength and sorcery. His <P2> Fissure Slice skill can damage even distant enemies.
His Glacier Strike ability lobs great lumps of ice at foes, and temporarily imbues his blade with an icy enchantment for extra damage<FG>
To learn more about spells and abilities for each character, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Desdemona uses her enormous axe to hack and slash her way through the fray. She'll keep swinging for as long as you hold <P2>.
Her Scrap Mettle skill devastates the defence and agility of her enemies, making her a useful ally when fighting powerful foes<FG>
Stringing stinging attacks together is Tsarevna Alena's stock-in-trade. Hold <P2> to make her Knuckle Sandwiches hit even harder<FG>
Her mega-fast Multifists attack deals massive damage with a blistering barrage of combo-boosting blows<FG>
Kiryl is a skilful and surprisingly strong spear-swinger with continuous, far-reaching strikes and other impressive abilities to boot.
This dependable defender can use Kabuff to boost his buddies' defence<MV>an absolute Goddess-send in boss battles<FG>
To learn more about Alena and Kiryl's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Torneko packs both a punch and a paunch, in the form of an almighty abacus and the belly-busting <P2> Charge ability<FG>
Being a merchant, he's got plenty of items at his disposal, not to mention the formidable forward-thrusting Flail of Destruction skill.
To learn more about each character's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Meena is a tarot tactician who marks her targets with a carefully aimed card strike, then follows up with a flurry of other attacks.
The Tower is a formidable skill that summons an almighty bolt of lightning to strike her mark<MV>and any nearby enemies as well<FG>
To learn more about Meena's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
A soaring starlet whose aptitude for aerial attacks allows her to hover when she racks up 100 hits or more.
Her ability to unleash spells and skills from above and below lets her dance deftly across the battlefield, dealing damage as she goes.
To learn more about Maya's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Carver is a burly brawler who beats down baddies with his fists and feet. Hold down <P3> and <P2> to ramp up the power of his attacks<FG>
His Knuckle Sandwich skill lets him muster his strength, then unleash a devastating punch that can damage even distant enemies<FG>
Terry is a skilled swordsman with a super-fast, far-reaching swing, who's equally comfortable in both attack and defence.
His Lightning Strike skill frazzles foes with its shocking strength, and fries mechanical meanies' circuits to bring them to a standstill<FG>
To learn more about Terry and Carver's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Maribel's boomerang is a wicked weapon on its own, but trigger Twomerang when she catches it, and you'll cause double the trouble<FG>
Her Crosscutter Throw skill lets her nip niftily backwards while attacking at the same time<MV>great for when you need a little space.
Ruff's a wild child with sharp claws that can make mincemeat of enemies, and a feral friend in the form of a ferocious wolf<FG>
His Ruff Rider attack has his canine cohort fly at foes and unleash a furious combo that can rip whole crowds of enemies to shreds.
To learn more about Ruff and Maribel's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Angelo is a hawk-eyed archer who can pierce his prey with pin-point precision. Holding <P3> charges up his arrows for stronger strikes.
With Shining Shot, he can let fly a flurry of light-infused arrows over an area<MV>perfect for punishing groups of aggressors.
Jessica's a whip-cracking warrior woman who can sweep whole swathes of foes off their feet with her all-encompassing attacks.
The swirling storms she whips up with Whipcrackle lay into enemies with lashing lightning bolts<MV>aim at groups for best results<FG>
To learn more about Jessica and Angelo's spells and abilities, open up the ‘Misc.’ menu and take a look at the manual.
Monster medals come in three different varieties<FI> Saviour, Sentry and Substitute.
Each type has its particular pros and cons<MV>give them all a go, and find out what works best for you<FG>
Talk to Patty to have her switch allies in and out of your party. You'll find her at the inn in Accordia.
Breakneck Bonuses are experience boosts earned by beating bigger baddies in double quick time.
The second your party draw their weapons, get slicing and dicing as quickly as you can and bag that bonus<FG>
Certain battles will need to be selected from the list you see when you visit the location. Sometimes more than one will be available.
During these battles, you won't be able to put your weapons away, so be sure to be good and ready before you go diving in<FG>
Use this screen to choose chat phrases to use while you're in multiplayer mode. You can set phrases for the inn and for battle separately.
When choosing phrases, you'll set up pages of five phrases each. There are four pages for use in the inn, and three for use in battle.
Now you can play using Flying Start mode<FG> Venture forth anew using an adventure log containing your completed game data.
You'll be able to start the story again, but with all the experience, equipment and money you earned the first time around<FG>
And as an added bonus, each party member and every vocation will start with 50 free skill points<FG>
If you want to change <F4><I0>00 or <F4><I0>10's vocation, you'll need to visit the Abbot of Alltrades.
New vocations will open up new weapons to try, new skills to master, and a whole range of new playing styles<FG>
But bear in mind that you'll need to start each new vocation from Level 1<MV>prepare to spend some time in training<FG>
Use the right stick to control the camera. You can also push <PG> to lock the camera on to certain enemies.
UNUSED
If you'd like to customise your camera settings, open up the menu and select ‘Misc.’, ‘Settings’, and then ‘Camera Settings’.
Some monsters have particular parts that are more vulnerable to attack than others.
Work out your enemies' weak spots, and wallop them where it hurts<FG>
You can allocate as many Party Powers as you like, as long as you don't exceed your current capacity.
Kazapple is a super-charged spell that has to be cast by all four of your party at once<MV>a kind of magical coup de grâce, if you will.
To use it, you'll need to have the ‘Knack of Kazapple’ Party Power activated.
Enact the Knack, and you can activate Kazapple like you would a Tag Trick.
Just press <PD> while holding down <PP> to offload everyone's tension in one go, and unleash the ultimate enchantment<FG>
UNUSED
Press <PI> to toggle the map in the top-right of the screen between a view of your surroundings and one of the entire area.
UNUSED
Objectives will be indicated on the map with flag icons.
In multiplayer modes, you can communicate with other players using a selection of preset phrases.
Hold <PD> to bring up a list at the bottom of the screen.
UNUSED
When the list is open, move the cursor with <P5> to choose the phrase you want to use, then press <P9> to send it.
Give it a whirl<MV>multiplayer's much more fun when everyone's interacting<FG>
Bonus balls are amazing objects that earn you double experience for a limited time only<FG> Open the menu and go to ‘Inventory’ to use one<FG>
Press <PD> while holding <PP> to ready yourself to cast Kazapple.
NOT USED
The rest of the party can then join in by doing the same.
NOT USED
When everyone's ready, the caster can use that magic button combination again to offload all your tension at once and let rip<FG>
NOT USED
You can choose whichever character, vocation and weapon type you wish. You can also set spells and abilities in advance.
To keep things fair, levels, equipment, skills and Party Powers won't count here, and your attributes will be set to predetermined values.
In Monster Medal Melee mode, you'll compete with other players to earn the most points in a duel with a dungeon master.
Damaging the dungeon master directly will boost your score a bit, but using monster medals is the way to win big<FG>
All three types of monster medal are available, so give them all a go and see what works best<FG>
And don't worry about being clobbered unconscious<MV>you'll be brought straight back to life to keep on clocking up the points<FG>
Your overall performance in monster medal melees will be reflected in the form of a ranking.
The better you do in a battle, the bigger the haul of rank-improving points. And using the Traveller's Tome will earn you even more<FG>
Usually, you'll be competing with combatants of a similar rank, but if you go via the inn, you can find opponents of all abilities.
Now you can play with people from all over the world<FG>
But if you only want to play with people from nearby, you can change the ‘Multiplayer Region’ option under ‘Online Settings’.
